questions.prompt: All cats are animals. All animals are living things. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: No cat is a living thing
Some animals are not living things

questions.explanation: Chaining the two universal statements, every cat is an animal and every animal is a living thing, so every cat is a living thing. The reverse claim about living things does not follow.

questions.prompt: All books are papers. Some pens are books. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The pens that are books must be papers, since all books are papers, so at least some pens are papers. Nothing forces all pens to be papers.

questions.prompt: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Does 'Some roses fade quickly' follow?
questions.explanation: The flowers that fade quickly might all be non-roses, so nothing links roses to fading. The conclusion is possible but not guaranteed, so it does not follow.

questions.prompt: No dog is a cat. All cats are pets. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: Cats are pets and no cat is a dog, so those cats are pets that are not dogs, hence some pets are not dogs. Dogs could still be pets, so 'no pet is a dog' is too strong.

questions.prompt: If it rains, the ground gets wet. The ground is not wet. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: If rain always makes the ground wet, then a dry ground proves it did not rain. This valid form is called modus tollens; denying the consequent denies the antecedent.
